def safe_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when name is a plain single file name that stays inside notes: non-empty, not "." or "..", with no "/" or "\\" separators, no NUL character and no drive colon."""
    ex safe_name("a.txt") == True
    ex safe_name("") == False
    ex safe_name(".") == False
    ex safe_name("..") == False
    ex safe_name("../secret.txt") == False
    ex safe_name("/etc/passwd") == False
    ex safe_name("sub/a.txt") == False
    ex safe_name("..\\x") == False
    ex safe_name("C:x") == False
    if name == "" or name == "." or name == "..":
        return False
    if "/" in name or "\\" in name or ":" in name or "\0" in name:
        return False
    return True

def first_readable(names: list[str]) -> str uses fs:
    """Text of the first file in names that can be read from the directory notes, or "" when none can.
    Names are untrusted. The body runs inside `with fs = fs.sub("notes"):` so only files under notes are reachable, and skips every name for which safe_name is False. A missing or unreadable file is skipped."""
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        for name in names:
            if not safe_name(name):
                continue
            text = fs.read_text(name) else ""
            if text != "":
                return text
    return ""
